overall: The AG found the Westminster Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving October 13 minutes that omitted a list of documents used, but found the minutes otherwise accurate and ordered an amendment.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 13 minutes inaccurately summarized the discussion of the Kiwi Court subdivision plan and public comment on it.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that the Board substantially complied with the requirement that it provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that occurred during the October 13 meeting regarding the subdivision plan for Kiwi Court.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 13 minutes failed to include a list of documents used at the meeting, such as the subdivision plans and a Conservation Agent letter.
allegations.key_passage: However, we find that the minutes of the October 13 meeting fail to include a list of documents used during the meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes said a member of the public submitted documents (attached) but none were attached to the minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, the Open Meeting Law does not require that documents used during a meeting and referenced in meeting minutes be appended to or stored with the minutes.

remedy: Within 60 days of receipt of the determination, amend the October 13 minutes to include a list of documents used during the meeting, and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
remedy_passage: We order the Board, within 60 days of receipt of this determination, to amend the minutes of the October 13 meeting to include a list of documents used during the meeting, and to certify to our office that it has done so.
